title: Arranging after Hines, and favorite arrangers

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Let's talk about arranging a bit. Did you do much arranging after you left Earl?
You just sort of wrote whatever band you were in -- you --
Yeah. Well, after I left Earl, got me working with small bands, there wasn't much need of an arranger.
Well, did bands other than those that you were working with, did they ever sound you about arrangements?
You just wrote for whoever you were working with?

Who influenced you in arranging, if anybody? There are so many things -- like I was talking last week about the sax solely on one of the tunes that you arranged. It sounds very much like Fletcher Henderson. Did you listen to other arrangers, and say, gee, I'd like to do something like that? Say a Fletcher Henderson arrangement?
Yeah, that's right. Fletcher Henderson, and Duke, and a lot of the big bands.
Yeah, because of the voicings and --
Because of the voicing he had. I tried to get that voicing, but that's kind of hard to do.
I was driving home this morning from the gig, and Dick Buckley was playing broadcasts from
1940 of the Ellington band. My, my, my, what a band that was.
Did you hear that band very much?
Yeah, I heard them a lot.
